land.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Powys, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands

predecessors.note: The page gives no founding year; it says Powys 'emerged during the Middle Ages following the end of Roman rule in Britain'. The start year is Cliopatria's.

successors.note: Division of 1160 'along the River Rhaeadr' (Powys page); Cliopatria starts Powys Fadog in 1169, so 1161-1168 is a gap between the two dossiers.
Same division; Cliopatria starts Powys Wenwynwyn in 1169.

capitals.name: Caer Guricon (Wroxeter, Viroconium Cornoviorum)
capitals.note: The page says Viroconium 'could have been the Powys capital' and that Brochwel Ysgithrog 'may have moved the court from Caer Guricon to Pengwern'; no years given, 540-549 is a bridge.

capitals.name: Pengwern (Shrewsbury)
capitals.note: Pengwern 'likely included at least Shrewsbury (Amwythig)'; the Powys page lists Brochwel as c. 550. The Pengwern page puts the court there 'in the 6th and 7th Century, before its establishment at Mathrafal, further west'.

capitals.name: Mathrafal (near Meifod)
capitals.note: 'The court was moved to Mathrafal Castle in the valley of the river Vyrnwy by 717.' Coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Cynan Garwyn
rulers.note: The page's list, which it says cannot be considered certain; entries with an open end (Eiludd 616-?, Beli c. 655) are left out.

rulers.name: Cyngen ap Cadell
rulers.note: Died 854 on the Powys page, 855 on the Pillar of Eliseg page.

rulers.name: Rhodri Mawr
rulers.note: Of Gwynedd; the page lists him under the dynasty of Manaw.

rulers.name: Bleddyn ap Cynfyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn
rulers.title: joint kings (Mathrafal line)

rulers.name: Cadwgan ap Bleddyn (with Iorwerth and Maredudd)
rulers.note: Page: 'Iorwerth ap Bleddyn (1075-1103, part); Cadwgan ap Bleddyn (1075-1111, part)'; the kingdom was divided between three of Bleddyn's sons in 1075 (Cadwgan page).

keyframe_review.note: 540-616, 5,787 km2. The Powys page gives no infobox area (it says only that Powys 'very roughly covered the northern two-thirds of the modern county of Powys'), so no ratio can be taken. The shape's east edge (lon -2.73) just reaches Shrewsbury, where the Pengwern page puts the court ('likely included at least Shrewsbury (Amwythig), and reached to the River Tern'); Wroxeter lies outside it.

617-625, 5,917 km2, 130 km2 more than the 540 shape and unexplained. The Battle of Chester (613-616) killed Selyf of Powys but the page reports no territorial change ('Instead Æthelfrith may have been planning to attack Powys'); shape left as drawn.
626-627, 5,852 km2: the north edge is cut from lat 53.06 to 52.99. No opened page reports a Powys loss in 626; unverified: page budget.
628-632, 5,723 km2, a second small trim of the north. Penda took the Severn valley from Wessex in 628 (Penda page) but no page names a Powys loss; unverified: page budget.

633-704, 5,787 km2, the 540 shape again. Powys forces 'may also have been present at the Battle of Maes Cogwy in 642' and had 'successful campaigns against the English in 655'; the page reports no change of border.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 705-853 only; the eastern trim toward Pengwern/Shrewsbury is dated by the pages only to 'the reign of Offa' and the dykes

keyframe_review.note: 705-859 in Cliopatria, 4,359 km2: the east is cut back (lon -2.73 to -2.87). Years: this dossier ends the shape at 853 because Rhodri Mawr became king of Powys on Cyngen's death in 854 and Cliopatria's Gwynedd takes the land in 860; 854-859 belong to Gwynedd. The 705 start is Cliopatria's and no opened page dates it: the Pengwern page says part of the Pengwern region 'remained in Welsh hands until the reign of Offa of Mercia', the Powys page has Wat's Dyke built after Elisedd's successes and Offa 'attacked Powys in 760 at Hereford', and the Wat's Dyke page gives the dyke as 'previously thought' early 8th century, '792-852' by the 2006 excavation, 'likely' the 820s. The shape is right for the 9th century; the cut may be 50-100 years later than 705. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 705..853 from this entry's own 'valid 705-853 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

878-899, 4,359 km2. Rhodri Mawr was killed in 878 (Rhodri page: 'slew Rhodri together with his son Gwriad'); Powys has its own king again, Merfyn ap Rhodri (878-900, Powys list). The infobox 'Conquest of Powys by the Second Dynasty of Gwynedd: before 886' is the page's own date for the union.

correction.text: Powys as in 878-899 and 911-921, 4,359 km2; Llywelyn ap Merfyn king 900-942 (page list)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 900-910: Cliopatria has no Powys shape for these eleven years, but the Powys page's list gives Llywelyn ap Merfyn as king 900-942 and nothing ends the kingdom. Shape taken from the 878 and 911 shapes (all 4,359 km2). Cliopatria's Seisyllwg grows from 4,512 to 8,914 km2 in 900; whether it absorbs Powys is not stated by any page opened (check against the Seisyllwg dossier).
911-921, 4,359 km2, the same as 878-899; unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 922-941 only; Hywel Dda takes Powys from Llywelyn ap Merfyn in 942

keyframe_review.note: 922-946 in Cliopatria, 4,272 km2. Years: the Powys page says Hywel Dda 'apparently took Powys from Llywelyn ap Merfyn' in 942, and Cliopatria's Powys row is absent from 947, when Seisyllwg grows to 18,353 km2. This dossier ends the independent shape at 941. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 922..941 from this entry's own 'valid 922-941 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

960-1039, 4,359 km2. The Powys list shows Owain ap Hywel (950-986), Maredudd ap Owain, Llywelyn ap Seisyll, Rhydderch and Iago as kings of Powys, all Welsh overlords; the page does not say when Powys became separate again, so the 960 return is Cliopatria's.

correction.text: Powys under Bleddyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn, the Mathrafal line, as the 960-1039 shape (4,359 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1063-1084: Cliopatria has no Powys shape for 1040-1084 (Gwynedd's shape grows to 10,634-10,721 km2 and holds it). The Powys list gives Gruffydd ap Llywelyn 1039-1063 and then the Mathrafal line, Bleddyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn from 1063; the Norman invasion page says Gruffydd was killed by his own men in 1063. From 1063 Powys is drawn again as in 960-1039 (4,359 km2); 1040-1062 stay in Gwynedd's shape. Overlaps Cliopatria's Gwynedd 1066-1084.

1085-1093, 2,490 km2: the shape loses the east (1,870 km2) to the Normans: 'By 1086 the Norman Earl Roger de Montgomery of Shrewsbury had built a castle at the Severn ford of Rhydwhiman.' The page dates the castle, not the loss; shape left as drawn.

1099-1151, 4,458 km2: after the Welsh revolt of 1094 and the Norman expedition of 1098, Cadwgan 'was able to reclaim part of Powys' the following year; he was 'sole ruler of the parts of Powys not in Norman hands' in 1103. The shape reaches lat 53.26 and lon -4.07, further north and west than any earlier shape. 1094-1098 stay a gap here and a contested zone in the ledger.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1152-1160 only; Powys is divided in 1160 between Madog's sons, Owain Cyfeiliog and Iorwerth Goch

keyframe_review.note: 1152-1168 in Cliopatria, 4,458 km2, unchanged from 1099. Years: Madog died about 9 February 1160 and 'Powys was never reunited, splitting into Powys Fadog (Lower Powys) and Powys Wenwynwyn (Upper Powys)'; this dossier ends the shape at 1160 (the Powys infobox also says 1160) and Cliopatria's successors start in 1169. About 1150 Owain Gwynedd took Madog's lands in Iâl and in 1157 Madog 'regained many Welsh lands'; the shape is not changed for either. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1152..1160 from this entry's own 'valid 1152-1160 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: very roughly the northern two-thirds of the modern county of Powys, with the Severn plain around Pengwern

ledger.note: 540: the Gwertherion kingdom of Powys is on the map. The page gives no founding year ('emerged ... following the end of Roman rule in Britain', 'ruled by the Gwertherion dynasty'; its genealogy puts Cadell Ddyrnllwg at c. 447-460 and Mawgan ap Pasgen at 'c. 540?'), so the year is Cliopatria's.
c. 550: Brochwel Ysgithrog 'may have moved the court from Caer Guricon to Pengwern' (Shrewsbury); the page lists him as c. 550 and gives no date for the move.

region.text: the eastern fringe of Powys toward Pengwern and the Severn (1,430 km2)

ledger.note: 705: the Cliopatria shape loses its eastern edge toward Pengwern to Mercia. No opened page dates this: Pengwern 'seems to have been shared between Mercia and Powys' and 'part of it remained in Welsh hands until the reign of Offa of Mercia'; the Powys page has Æthelbald build Wat's Dyke after Elisedd's successes and says Offa 'attacked Powys in 760 at Hereford'; the Wat's Dyke page dates the dyke early 8th century (older view), 792-852 (2006 dig), 'likely' the 820s. The year 705 is Cliopatria's.
By 717: the court moves west to Mathrafal in the Vyrnwy valley. 'The court was moved to Mathrafal Castle in the valley of the river Vyrnwy by 717.'

region.text: the whole kingdom, joined to Gwynedd under Rhodri Mawr

ledger.note: 854: Cyngen dies and Rhodri Mawr of Gwynedd becomes king of Powys. 'With the death of Cyngen in 854 Rhodri Mawr became king of Powys'; the Pillar of Eliseg page says Cyngen died in 855. Cliopatria's Powys shape runs to 859 and Gwynedd's grows to 10,721 km2 in 860 (6,364 + 4,359).
854: the Gwertherion line of Powys ends with Cyngen ap Cadell and the page's list passes to the dynasty of Manaw, Rhodri Mawr and his sons. Same state, same colour.

878: Powys has its own king again after Rhodri Mawr's death. The list gives 'Merfyn ap Rhodri (878-900)'; Rhodri was killed in a campaign by Ceolwulf of Mercia in 878 (Rhodri page). Cliopatria's Gwynedd falls back to 6,364 km2 in 878.

942: Hywel Dda takes Powys. 'He apparently took Powys from Llywelyn ap Merfyn at the same time' as Gwynedd; Hywel (942-950) and Owain ap Hywel (950-986) head the list of kings of Powys. Cliopatria keeps the shape to 946 and joins the land to Seisyllwg (18,353 km2) from 947.
960: Powys is a separate shape again. The page does not say how or when Powys came apart from Hywel Dda's realm; the year is Cliopatria's (Seisyllwg's row ends 959, Gwynedd's resumes 960).

1039: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn heads the list of Welsh kings of Powys (1039-1063) and Cliopatria folds Powys into Gwynedd's shape from 1040 (10,634 km2). The page does not say that Gruffydd conquered Powys; the reading is mine.

1063: Powys passes to the Mathrafal line. Gruffydd ap Llywelyn 'was turned upon by his own men, who killed him in 1063' (Norman invasion page); the Powys list gives Bleddyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn for 1063-1075. Cliopatria folds Powys into Gwynedd until 1084.
1063: Bleddyn and Rhiwallon ap Cynfyn found the Mathrafal line, the page's third dynasty of Powys. Same state, same colour.

region.text: the Severn plain and eastern Powys around Rhydwhiman (Montgomery)

ledger.note: By 1086: the Normans take the east. 'By 1086 the Norman Earl Roger de Montgomery of Shrewsbury had built a castle at the Severn ford of Rhydwhiman.' Cliopatria shows Powys again from 1085 at 2,490 km2 (Norman England has a new 1085 shape). In 1075 the kingdom was divided between three of Bleddyn's sons (Cadwgan page).

region.text: Powys of 1085-1093 and the land the Welsh fought for

ledger.note: 1094: Welsh revolt against the Normans. 'In 1094 a Welsh revolt against Norman rule broke out'; Rhys ap Tewdwr had been killed in 1093 and the Normans, not the Welsh, gained most. Cliopatria shows no Powys 1094-1098 and a larger Norman England; the zone is drawn contested.

region.text: Powys of 1085-1093 and the land the Welsh fought for

ledger.note: 1099: the fighting over Powys ends with Cadwgan's return; the page gives 1098 for the Norman invasion and the following year for the return.

1099: Cadwgan recovers part of Powys. 'Cadwgan was able to reclaim part of Powys'; in 1103 he was 'sole ruler of the parts of Powys not in Norman hands'. Cliopatria's 1099 shape (4,458 km2) reaches lat 53.26 and lon -4.07.

region.text: the whole kingdom, shared between Madog's sons, Owain Cyfeiliog and Iorwerth Goch

ledger.note: 1160: Powys is divided. Madog ap Maredudd died about 9 February 1160 and 'Powys was never reunited, splitting into Powys Fadog (Lower Powys) and Powys Wenwynwyn (Upper Powys)'; the Powys page says the realm was divided along the River Rhaeadr (infobox: 'division between Northern and Southern Powys: 1160').

wars.name: Battle of Chester
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith of Northumbria 'annihilated a combined force from the Welsh kingdoms of Powys and Rhôs'; Selyf Sarffgadau of Powys was killed. No land changed hands on the page.
wars.note: Dated 613 in the Annals of Ulster (s.a. 612, recte 613) and 'around 615 or 616' by Plummer; the Powys page's infobox says 613 and its text 616. Cliopatria's Northumbria row starts 612; Æthelfrith is also covered by the Bernicia dossier.

wars.name: Battle of Maserfield
wars.outcome: Penda of Mercia defeated and killed Oswald of Northumbria on 5 August 642; Welsh poetry 'suggests that Penda fought in alliance with the men of Powys'. No border moved.

wars.name: Offa's attack on Powys (Battle of Hereford)
wars.outcome: 'Offa attacked Powys in 760 at Hereford.' No territorial result is given.
wars.note: Offa's Dyke itself is undated on the pages opened.

wars.name: Welsh revolt of 1094
wars.outcome: The rising of 1094 and the Norman invasion of 1098 end with Cadwgan reclaiming part of Powys in 1099 on homage to Earl Robert of Shrewsbury.

wars.name: Madog ap Maredudd and Owain Gwynedd
belligerents: Ranulf de Gernon, Earl of Chester

zones.text: Iâl, the lands Owain Gwynedd took from Madog

wars.outcome: 'In around 1150 Madog made an alliance with Ranulf de Gernon' before Owain Gwynedd defeated them near Ewloe and took Madog's lands in Iâl; in 1157 Madog backed Henry II's invasion of Gwynedd and 'regained many Welsh lands'.
wars.note: The page does not say whether Iâl was among the lands regained; the Cliopatria shape is not changed.

certainty.note: Welsh kingdom frontiers are approximate throughout; the eastern edge against Mercia is the one line with physical markers (Wat's Dyke, Offa's Dyke), whose dating is disputed, and it is still drawn soft.

notes:
Kingdom of Powys (13 Cliopatria shapes, 540-1168), written from nine pages (the Powys budget) plus the Penda page opened for the Hwicce dossier.
ROW NOT SPLIT: the brief suspects successive states in one 628-year row. The pages present one continuing kingdom (Gwertherion, Manaw and Mathrafal dynasties); the gaps in Cliopatria (860-877, 900-910, 947-959, 1040-1084, 1094-1098) are years when Powys sits inside Gwynedd's, Seisyllwg's or Norman England's shapes. They are handled as loss/gain events and two new keyframes (900-910, 1063-1084), not as separate states.
END 1160, NOT 1168: the Powys infobox and the Madog page date the division to 1160; Cliopatria's Powys row runs to 1168 and Powys Fadog/Wenwynwyn start 1169. Years 1161-1168 will be empty unless the successors' dossiers start in 1160. Orchestrator: check.
OVERLAPS TO CHECK: the Gwynedd dossier (Cliopatria Gwynedd 1066-1084 is 10,721 km2 and contains Powys); the Seisyllwg dossier (900-910 and 947-959); Norman England 1094-1098.
UNVERIFIED: the 626-632 trims, the 617 growth, the 705 start of the eastern cut (pages date it to Offa or the dykes, probably later than 705), the 960 return, the 1039 loss. A gap-filler should open Offa's Dyke, Hywel Dda, Gruffydd ap Llywelyn, Bleddyn ap Cynfyn, Powys Fadog and Powys Wenwynwyn.
DISAGREEMENTS: Cyngen died 854 (Powys page) or 855 (Pillar page); the Chester battle is 613 or 616; Cadwgan's death is 1103 in the Cadwgan infobox and 1111 in its text (1111 used).
GAZETTEER: region 'Iâl' (the cantref around Llangollen / Valle Crucis, lordship of Yale) is used in a war zone and is not in regions.jsonl.
